ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: From Napata, Piye and his successors united Nubia and Egypt as the Twenty-Fifth Dynasty, before Meroë became a great centre of iron.
Controlling the Red Sea port of Adulis, Aksum issued its own gold coins and conquered Kush around 350 CE.
The Soninke 'land of gold' taxed both salt moving south and gold moving north, reserving every gold nugget for the king.
The founder of Mali, whose victory at Kirina united the Manding chiefdoms and whose epic is still preserved by griots.
Mali controlled the goldfields of Bambuk and Bure and made Timbuktu and Djenné centres of trade and Islamic learning.
Mansa Musa's lavish spending of gold in Cairo in 1324 put Mali on the map, quite literally in the Catalan Atlas.
The largest empire in West African history, built by Sunni Ali and Askia Muhammad on the cities of Gao, Timbuktu and Djenné.
In 1591 a small Moroccan force armed with arquebuses routed a much larger Songhai army in a single engagement.
Osei Tutu I and the priest Okomfo Anokye united the Akan chiefdoms around the Golden Stool and defeated Denkyira at Feyiase in 1701.
